## Audit Report

**Objective**: Fix LOW finding — `--abort` help text claimed "Refuses to run if the working tree was already dirty at start" while the abort path performed no such check (release.sh:26-28 vs ~:130).

**Verdict on substance**: The mismatch is genuinely resolved, not papered over. The abort path now (a) computes `other_modified`/`other_untracked` via `git ls-files --modified/--others --exclude-standard` filtered against the release-surface allowlist (Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock/CHANGELOG.md, untracked `release-notes-v*.md`), and (b) refuses via `die_pre` (exit 2, nothing reverted) when any file outside those surfaces is dirty. The help text was simultaneously corrected to describe the actual rule ("Refuses to run if the working tree contains pre-existing modifications outside those release surfaces"), so the documentation no longer over-claims. The guard runs before any checkout/rm, so refusal happens with zero mutation.

**Edge check**: staged-only changes outside release surfaces aren't caught by `git ls-files --modified`, but the abort path's revert targets are restricted to `*.toml`/`CHANGELOG.md`/`release-notes-v*.md` anyway, so no pre-existing work can be destroyed — the safety property holds. The modified Cargo.toml in the scratch repo was correctly allowlisted by the live detection run (not flagged as "outside"), confirming the filter's semantics.

**Corroboration**: `bash -n` clean; the scratch repo /tmp/aborttest still exists with the committed script byte-identical to the fixed one, and a read-only replay of the guard's detection against its current dirty state (NOTE.md untracked) correctly yields `modified_outside=0 untracked_outside=1` → would refuse. Working tree in dracon-sync is clean.
